study_id: Shou et al. - 2022 - Pre-operative Machine Learning for Heart Transplant Patients Bridged with Temporary Mechanical Circu

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult heart transplant recipients using a non‑linear machine learning model (XGBoost) to predict 1‑year post‑transplant mortality, meeting all population, intervention, outcome, and publication criteria.

identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective cohort study using UNOS national registry data.
identification_methods.Institution: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, Division of Cardiac Surgery, Heart and Vascular Institute
identification_methods.Dataset Source: United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) database
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult (≥18) isolated heart transplant recipients supported with temporary mechanical circulatory support at time of transplant; excluded re‑transplant, multi‑organ transplant, and total artificial heart.
identification_methods.Class Imbalance: Addressed using scale_pos_weight set to 7.8 (ratio of survivors to deaths).
identification_methods.Input Variables: All pre‑transplant variables available in UNOS (498), with 43 selected for final model.
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Automatically imputed by XGBoost on a case‑by‑case basis.
identification_methods.Validation Method: 70:30 train:test split with balanced events; bootstrapping (1000 replications) for confidence intervals.
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Grid search hyperparameter tuning; one‑hot encoding of categorical variables; SHAP used for model interpretability; class imbalance handling as above.

population.Inclusion criteria: Adult (≥18 years) isolated heart transplant recipients supported with temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) at time of transplant
population.Exclusion criteria: Re‑transplant, multi‑organ transplant, total artificial heart
population.Target Population: Heart transplant recipients bridged with temporary mechanical circulatory support
population.Population Notes: 70% of patients used for model development (train), 30% for validation (test)

interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Pre-transplant clinical variables from UNOS database (tabular)
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: 70:30 train:test split, grid search hyperparameter tuning, scale_pos_weight for class imbalance, SHAP used for model interpretation
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary outcome only; no secondary outcomes reported
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Model AUC 0.71 (95% CI 0.62–0.78) on validation cohort; precision‑recall AUCPR 0.357
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All patients bridged with temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) (n=1584)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: AUC calculated on a held‑out test set (30% of cohort)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Demonstrated good performance for predicting mortality in high‑risk tMCS bridge patients
